newsitem.title: USA: Cooper says Q1 hurt by European economy.
newsitem.headline: Cooper says Q1 hurt by European economy.

text.p: Cooper Industries Inc said Wednesday that its first quarter results were hurt by a weak European economy that affected all of its businesses.
The company said its electrical products, tools and hardware, and automotive products segments had weaker sales in Europe during the quarter.

"While we have some concerns about the domestic economy and the anticipated recovery in Europe, we expect 1997 will be a very good year for Cooper Industries," Chairman, President and Chief Executive H. John Riley said in a statement.

For the first quarter, Cooper reported net income of $77.7 million, or $0.67 per fully diluted share, on revenue of $1.32 billion. In the prior year's first quarter, the company reported net income of $62.1 million, or $0.56 per fully diluted share, on revenues of $1.29 billion.

In the electrical products segment, the company said that significant increases from North American sales of fuses, power equipment and lighting more than offset the effect that a soft European economy had on the circuit protection and enclosure businesses.

It said that its tools and hardware sales remained strong for power tool products, particularly to customers in the aerospace and automotive industries, while demand for hand tools and window treatment products was off in both North America and Europe.
Revenues in the automotive products segment were off slightly, due to a continued sluggish domestic and European aftermarket, Cooper Industries said.
